key_insight: This paper tests whether dense, token-by-token guidance from a stronger teacher helps a smaller model reach a target accuracy with less training compute than GRPO reinforcement learning. The supplied abstract is truncated, so it does not establish which method wins.
problem_solved: Practitioners need compute-aware evidence to choose between teacher-guided on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning, rather than comparing accuracy alone.
method: Compare vanilla reverse-KL on-policy distillation, using student-generated rollouts and a frozen teacher's per-token supervision, against Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Measure held-out accuracy against training FLOPs to assess the compute required to reach a target accuracy.
Vary task difficulty, student and teacher sizes, domain, and optimization choices.
impact: The comparison provides a framework for evaluating when teacher supervision is worth its computational cost. Specific efficiency gains and practical recommendations cannot be confirmed from the incomplete abstract.
visual_elements: Side-by-side training diagrams: student rollouts with frozen-teacher token supervision versus GRPO reinforcement learning.

paper_title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
paper_authors: Zeyu Leo Liu, Yang Li, Bo Pang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xuan-Phi Nguyen
